          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14
      - uses: *ul
        with:
          name: binding-manifest
          path: dist-bindings/binding-packages.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  assemble:
    name: Verify complete release payload
    needs: [plan, check, build, bindings]
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    env: { LABEL: "${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}" }
    steps:
      - *co1
      - *py
      - uses: &dl actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with: { pattern: "binary-*", path: dist, merge-multiple: true }
      - name: Check every target and add source archive and checksums
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release rshellcheck-release assemble --label "${LABEL}"
      - uses: *dl
        with: { pattern: "binding-*", path: dist, merge-multiple: true }
      - name: Verify all binding distributions and their source identity
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m binding_packages verify dist
      - *node26
      - name: Package native npm binaries and launcher
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_packages build dist --label "${LABEL}"
      - name: Test native npm installation without install scripts
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_packages test dist
      - name: Build and install native Python wheels
        run: |
          uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels build dist --label "${LABEL}"
          uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels test dist
      - name: Prepare exact released source for SBOM scanning
        run: mkdir -p sbom-source && tar -xzf "dist/rshellcheck-${LABEL}-source.tar.gz" -C sbom-source --strip-components=1
      - name: Generate source dependency SBOM
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
        env:
          SYFT_SOURCE_NAME: rshellcheck
          SYFT_SOURCE_VERSION: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
        with:
          path: sbom-source
          format: spdx-json
          syft-version: v1.54.0
          output-file: dist/source.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: false
          upload-release-assets: false
          dependency-snapshot: false
      - name: Validate SBOM and checksum the complete payload
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release rshellcheck-supply-chain dist --lockfile sbom-source/Cargo.lock
      - uses: *ul
        with:
          name: rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
          path: dist/*
          overwrite: true
          if-no-files-found: error
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 14

  registry-payload:
    permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }
    name: Repackage verified release for registries
    needs: plan
    if: needs.plan.outputs.registry_only == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' && !(inputs.registry == 'npm' && inputs.artifact_run_id != '')
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    env:
      REGISTRY: ${{ inputs.registry }}
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    steps:
      - *co0
      - *py
      - *node26
      - uses: *dl
        if: inputs.artifact_run_id != ''
        with:
          name: rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ inputs.artifact_run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Verify original signatures, package and smoke-test
        if: inputs.artifact_run_id == ''
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m registry_payload dist
      - name: Verify resumed payload checksums and source identity
        if: inputs.artifact_run_id != ''
        run: |
          (cd dist && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
          uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m binding_packages verify dist
          uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_packages verify dist
          if [[ "${REGISTRY}" != npm ]]; then
            if [[ ! -f dist/native-wheels.json ]]; then
              uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels build dist
              uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels test dist
              (cd dist && sha256sum rshellcheck-*-py3-none-*.whl native-wheels.json >> SHA256SUMS)
            fi
            uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels verify dist
          fi
      - uses: *ul
        with:
          name: rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
          path: dist/*
          if-no-files-found: error
          compression-level: 0
          retention-days: 14

  publish:
    name: Publish complete GitHub release
    needs: [plan, assemble]
    if: needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs'
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions: { contents: write, id-token: write, attestations: write }
    env:
      GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
      TAG: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.tag }}
      LABEL: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
    steps:
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - name: Verify checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
      - name: Sign SLSA build provenance for every payload file
        id: provenance
        uses: actions/attest@4d7d407517fe0a9f57ab8ca277dfd2efb1188c7f # main
        with: { subject-path: dist/* }
      - name: Attest the source dependency inventory
        id: sbom
        uses: actions/attest@4d7d407517fe0a9f57ab8ca277dfd2efb1188c7f # main
        with:
          subject-path: dist/rshellcheck-${{ env.LABEL }}-source.tar.gz
          sbom-path: dist/source.spdx.json
      - name: Verify signatures and workflow identity before publishing
        env:
          PROVENANCE_BUNDLE: ${{ steps.provenance.outputs.bundle-path }}
          SBOM_BUNDLE: ${{ steps.sbom.outputs.bundle-path }}
        run: |
          identity=(--repo "${GH_REPO}" --signer-workflow "${GH_REPO}/.github/workflows/release.yml"
            --source-digest "${GITHUB_SHA}" --source-ref "${GITHUB_REF}")
          for asset in dist/*; do
            gh attestation verify "${asset}" --bundle "${PROVENANCE_BUNDLE}" "${identity[@]}"
          done
          gh attestation verify "dist/rshellcheck-${LABEL}-source.tar.gz" \
            --bundle "${SBOM_BUNDLE}" --predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3 "${identity[@]}"
          cp "${PROVENANCE_BUNDLE}" dist/provenance.sigstore.json
          cp "${SBOM_BUNDLE}" dist/source-sbom.sigstore.json
      - name: Upload to a draft, then publish
        run: |
          # Recover an interrupted draft; never overwrite a published release.
          if gh release view "${TAG}" --json isDraft > release.json 2> release-error.txt; then
            jq -e '.isDraft == true' release.json
          else
            # An auth/network error must not be mistaken for a missing release.
            if ! grep -qi 'release not found' release-error.txt; then
              cat release-error.txt >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            flags=()
            if [[ "${LABEL}" == *-* ]]; then flags+=(--prerelease); fi
            gh release create "${TAG}" --verify-tag --draft \
              --title "rshellcheck ${LABEL}" --generate-notes "${flags[@]}"
          fi
          gh release upload "${TAG}" dist/* --clobber
          gh release view "${TAG}" --json assets > release.json
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import json
          from pathlib import Path
          expected = {p.name for p in Path("dist").iterdir()}
          actual = {asset["name"] for asset in json.loads(Path("release.json").read_text())["assets"]}
          if actual != expected:
              raise SystemExit(f"Release assets differ: missing={expected - actual}, extra={actual - expected}")
          PY
          # Publication happens only after every upload completes.
          gh release edit "${TAG}" --draft=false
          gh release view "${TAG}" --json url,isDraft > release.json
          jq -e '.isDraft == false' release.json
          jq -r '.url' release.json

  container:
    name: Package CLI container
    needs: [plan, assemble, registry-payload]
    if: ${{ (inputs.registry == '' || inputs.registry == 'all') && !cancelled() && (needs.assemble.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions: { contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, attestations: write }
    env:
      LABEL: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
      SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/kjanat/shellcheck-rs
      PUBLISH: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    steps:
      - *co1
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - name: Prepare verified static binaries
        shell: bash
        run: |
          (cd dist && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
          for pair in amd64:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl arm64:aarch64-unknown-linux-musl 386:i686-unknown-linux-musl arm:armv7-unknown-linux-musleabihf; do
            arch="${pair%%:*}"
            target="${pair#*:}"
            mkdir -p "docker/cli/${arch}"
            tar -xzf "dist/rshellcheck-${LABEL}-${target}.tar.gz" --strip-components=1 \
              -C "docker/cli/${arch}" "rshellcheck-${LABEL}-${target}/rshellcheck"
          done
          cp LICENSE docker/cli/LICENSE.txt
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
      - name: Smoke-test CLI image
        run: |
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --load -t rshellcheck-test docker/cli
          docker run --rm rshellcheck-test --version
          printf '#!/bin/sh\necho ok\n' > docker/cli/clean.sh
          docker run --rm -v "${PWD}/docker/cli:/w:ro" rshellcheck-test clean.sh
          # shellcheck disable=SC2016
          printf '#!/bin/sh\necho $var\n' > docker/cli/warning.sh
          status=0
          docker run --rm -v "${PWD}/docker/cli:/w:ro" rshellcheck-test -f quiet warning.sh || status=$?
          test "${status}" -eq 1
      - uses: &dockerLogin docker/login-action@8aa5831fb8d48d8f76594c7ddde61ae58019f550 # v4.8.0
        if: env.PUBLISH == 'true'
        with: &dockerLoginOptions { registry: ghcr.io, username: "${{ github.actor }}", password: "${{ github.token }}" }
      - name: Build multi-platform image
        id: image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          args=(--output "type=oci,dest=cli-image.tar")
          if [[ "${PUBLISH}" == true ]]; then
            args=(--push --tag "${IMAGE}:${LABEL}")
            if [[ "${LABEL}" != *-* ]]; then args+=(--tag "${IMAGE}:latest"); fi
          fi
          docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64,linux/386,linux/arm/v7 \
            --label "org.opencontainers.image.version=${LABEL}" \
            --label "org.opencontainers.image.revision=${SOURCE_COMMIT}" \
            --provenance=mode=max --sbom=true --metadata-file image.json "${args[@]}" docker/cli
          digest="$(jq -er '."containerimage.digest"' image.json)"
          echo "digest=${digest}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
      - name: Attest published image
        if: env.PUBLISH == 'true'
        uses: actions/attest@4d7d407517fe0a9f57ab8ca277dfd2efb1188c7f # main
        with:
          subject-name: ghcr.io/kjanat/shellcheck-rs
          subject-digest: ${{ steps.image.outputs.digest }}
          push-to-registry: false

  binary-images:
    name: Package copy-only binary images
    needs: [plan, assemble, registry-payload]
    if: ${{ (inputs.registry == '' || inputs.registry == 'all') && !cancelled() && (needs.assemble.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, packages: write }
    env:
      LABEL: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
      TARGETS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.matrix }}
      SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      IMAGE: ghcr.io/kjanat/shellcheck-rs/binaries
      PUBLISH: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    steps:
      - *co1
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
      - uses: *dockerLogin
        if: env.PUBLISH == 'true'
        with: *dockerLoginOptions
      - name: Package and verify every binary without executing it
        shell: bash
        run: |
          (cd dist && sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS)
          targets="$(jq -er '.include[].target' <<< "${TARGETS}")"
          while IFS= read -r target; do
            stem="rshellcheck-${LABEL}-${target}"
            context="${RUNNER_TEMP}/binary-${target}"
            mkdir -p "${context}/payload"
            cp docker/binaries/Dockerfile docker/binaries/.dockerignore "${context}/"
            binary=rshellcheck
            if [[ "${target}" == *windows* ]]; then
              binary=rshellcheck.exe
              for file in "${binary}" LICENSE.txt BUILD.json; do
                unzip -p "dist/${stem}.zip" "${stem}/${file}" > "${context}/payload/${file}"
              done
            else
              tar -xzf "dist/${stem}.tar.gz" --strip-components=1 -C "${context}/payload" \
                "${stem}/${binary}" "${stem}/LICENSE.txt" "${stem}/BUILD.json"
            fi
            chmod 755 "${context}/payload/${binary}"
            tag="${IMAGE}:${LABEL}-${target}"
            args=(--platform linux/amd64 --tag "${tag}"
              --label "org.opencontainers.image.version=${LABEL}"
              --label "org.opencontainers.image.revision=${SOURCE_COMMIT}"
              --label "io.rshellcheck.target=${target}")
            docker buildx build "${args[@]}" --load "${context}"
            container="$(docker create "${tag}")"
            trap 'docker rm "${container}" >/dev/null' EXIT
            for file in "${binary}" LICENSE.txt BUILD.json; do
              docker cp "${container}:/${file}" "${context}/copied"
              cmp "${context}/payload/${file}" "${context}/copied"
            done
            docker rm "${container}"
            trap - EXIT
            if [[ "${PUBLISH}" == true ]]; then
              docker buildx build "${args[@]}" --push --provenance=mode=max --sbom=true "${context}"
              docker buildx imagetools inspect "${tag}"
            fi
          done <<< "${targets}"

  npm-plan:
    name: Plan missing npm publications
    needs: [plan, publish, registry-payload]
    if: ${{ inputs.registry != 'pypi' && !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && (needs.publish.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success' || (needs.plan.outputs.registry_only == 'true' && inputs.registry == 'npm' && inputs.artifact_run_id != '')) && needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.npm.outputs.matrix }}
      native: ${{ steps.npm.outputs.native }}
      wasm: ${{ steps.npm.outputs.wasm }}
      launcher: ${{ steps.npm.outputs.launcher }}
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      NPM_PLAN: "true"
    steps: &NpmPublishSteps
      - *co0
      - uses: *node
        with: { node-version: "26", registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org" }
      - *py
      - uses: *dl
        with:
          name: rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ inputs.artifact_run_id || github.run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Verify complete payload checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
      - name: Plan or publish verified npm archive
        id: npm
        run: |
          if [[ "${NPM_PLAN:-false}" == true ]]; then uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m npm_publish dist --plan
          else uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m npm_publish dist --package "${NPM_PACKAGE}"
          fi

  npm:
    name: Publish ${{ matrix.package }}
    needs: [plan, npm-plan]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.npm-plan.result == 'success' && needs.npm-plan.outputs.native == 'true' }}
    strategy: { fail-fast: false, matrix: "${{ fromJSON(needs.npm-plan.outputs.matrix) }}" }
    env: { NPM_PACKAGE: "${{ matrix.package }}", RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: "${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}" }
    environment:
      name: npm
      url: https://www.npmjs.com/package/${{ matrix.package }}/v/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }
    steps: *NpmPublishSteps

  npm-wasm:
    name: Publish @kjanat/rshellcheck-wasm
    needs: [plan, npm-plan]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.npm-plan.result == 'success' && needs.npm-plan.outputs.wasm == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }
    environment:
      name: npm
      url: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kjanat/rshellcheck-wasm/v/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      NPM_PACKAGE: "@kjanat/rshellcheck-wasm"
    steps: *NpmPublishSteps

  npm-launcher:
    name: Publish @kjanat/rshellcheck
    needs: [plan, npm-plan, npm]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.npm-plan.result == 'success' && needs.npm-plan.outputs.launcher == 'true' && (needs.npm.result == 'success' || needs.npm-plan.outputs.native == 'false') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }
    environment:
      name: npm
      url: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kjanat/rshellcheck/v/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
      NPM_PACKAGE: "@kjanat/rshellcheck"
    steps: *NpmPublishSteps

  pypi:
    name: Publish Python bindings to PyPI
    needs: [plan, publish, registry-payload]
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/rshellcheck-wasm/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}/
    if: ${{ inputs.registry != 'npm' && !cancelled() && (needs.publish.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success') && needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }
    steps:
      - *co0
      - *py
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - name: Verify complete payload checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
      - name: Publish verified wheel and source distribution
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m binding_packages publish-pypi dist

  native-wheel-smoke:
    name: Native wheel on ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [plan, assemble, registry-payload]
    if: ${{ inputs.registry != 'npm' && !cancelled() && (needs.assemble.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success') }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        runner: [ubuntu-26.04, windows-2025, macos-15]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    timeout-minutes: 10
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
    steps:
      - *co0
      - *py
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - name: Install native wheel without network and run CLI checks
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels test dist

  pypi-native:
    name: Publish native Python wheels
    needs: [plan, publish, registry-payload, native-wheel-smoke]
    if: ${{ needs.native-wheel-smoke.result == 'success' && inputs.registry != 'npm' && !cancelled() && (needs.publish.result == 'success' || needs.registry-payload.result == 'success') && needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/rshellcheck/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}/
    env:
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
    steps:
      - *co0
      - *py
      - uses: *dl
        with: { name: "rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}", path: dist }
      - name: Verify complete payload checksums
        working-directory: dist
        run: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
      - name: Publish native wheels with trusted publishing
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m native_wheels publish dist

  upstream-aliases:
    name: Advance stable upstream aliases
    needs: [plan, npm-plan, npm, npm-wasm, npm-launcher, pypi, pypi-native, container, binary-images]
    env:
      REGISTRY: ${{ inputs.registry }}
      RELEASE_SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.commit }}
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.npm-plan.result == 'success' && (needs.npm.result == 'success' || needs.npm-plan.outputs.native == 'false') && (needs.npm-wasm.result == 'success' || needs.npm-plan.outputs.wasm == 'false') && (needs.npm-launcher.result == 'success' || needs.npm-plan.outputs.launcher == 'false') && (inputs.registry == 'npm' || (needs.pypi.result == 'success' && needs.pypi-native.result == 'success' && needs.container.result == 'success' && needs.binary-images.result == 'success')) && needs.plan.outputs.publish == 'true' && !contains(needs.plan.outputs.label, '-') && github.repository == 'kjanat/shellcheck-rs' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    environment:
      name: npm
      url: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@kjanat/rshellcheck/v/${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
    concurrency:
      group: release-upstream-aliases
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions: { contents: write, actions: read, packages: write, id-token: write }
    steps:
      - *co0
      - uses: *node
        with: { node-version: "26", registry-url: "https://registry.npmjs.org" }
      - run: npm install --global npm@12.2.0
      - *py
      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4.4.1
      - uses: *dockerLogin
        with: *dockerLoginOptions
      - uses: *dl
        with:
          name: rshellcheck-${{ needs.plan.outputs.label }}
          path: dist
          run-id: ${{ inputs.artifact_run_id || github.run_id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - name: Verify release payload
        working-directory: dist
        run: sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS
      - name: Promote upstream aliases and verify their targets
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: uv run --locked --no-dev --package rshellcheck-release python -m release_aliases dist

        run: go install "actionlint.kjanat.dev/v2/cmd/actionlint@${ref}";
          echo "${GOBIN}" >> "${GITHUB_PATH}"
      - run: actionlint plugin install shellcheck # `-v` INSTALL HAS NO VERBOSE... FFS
        if: false # ignore[if-cond]
      - run: actionlint check -v --network-stats
          --experimental -o github -o pretty --summary
          --no-tool shellcheck --no-tool ruff

  lint:
    name: "Format, clippy, workflows"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # dprint formats .rs and .toml through `mise exec -- rustfmt|tombi`, so the
    # toolchain comes from mise.toml. Binding runtimes are tested separately.
    env: { MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS: "python,node,go" }
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: *CO

      - name: Install the toolchain (mise)
        uses: jdx/mise-action@f5be966e4a917d54244728e6a5fdcd1d93a35e6c # v5.2.6

      - name: Check formatting
        uses: kjanat/dprint-check@b6a885d3403db5e40ed59f2c27917d758381f577 # v3.2.0

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo lint

  conformance-gate:
    name: Build and run gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - parallel:
          - name: Checkout repository
            uses: *CO
          - name: Remove shellcheck from runner
            run: sudo apt-get remove -y shellcheck 2>/dev/null || true

      - name: Install Rust stable
        id: rust
        uses: &rust dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: &CA actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6
        env: { CACHE_PREFIX: "${{ format('{0}-{1}-cargo-{2}', runner.os, runner.arch, steps.rust.outputs.cachekey) }}" }
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            target
          key: ${{ format('{0}-{1}-{2}', env.CACHE_PREFIX, hashFiles('Cargo.lock', '**/Cargo.toml', '.cargo/**'), hashFiles('crates/**')) }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ format('{0}-{1}-', env.CACHE_PREFIX, hashFiles('Cargo.lock', '**/Cargo.toml', '.cargo/**')) }}
            ${{ format('{0}-',     env.CACHE_PREFIX) }}

      - name: Test oracle cache validation
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -v

      - name: Fetch pinned upstream source
        env: { GH_TOKEN: "${{ github.token }}" }
        run: python3 tools/oracle.py --fetch-only

      - name: Cache Haskell oracle
        id: oracle
        uses: *CA
        with:
          path: |
            .cache/shellcheck-oracle
            .cache/shellcheck-oracle.json
          key: ${{ format('{0}-{1}-oracle-ghc{2}-{3}', runner.os, runner.arch, env.ghc-version, hashFiles('tools/oracle.json', 'tools/oracle.py')) }}

        id: haskell
        uses: haskell-actions/setup@0f8e8c99d88aeb3fbfd523f1ef2c6f762d10d64d # v2
        with: { ghc-version: "${{ env.ghc-version }}" }

      - name: Cache Haskell build
        if: *NoCacheHit
        uses: *CA
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ steps.haskell.outputs.cabal-store }}
            .cache/upstream-shellcheck/dist-newstyle
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-oracle-build-${{ env.ghc-version }}-${{ hashFiles('tools/oracle.json', 'tools/oracle.py') }}

      - name: Build Haskell oracle
        if: *NoCacheHit
        run: python3 tools/oracle.py

      - name: Verify cached oracle identity
        run: python3 tools/oracle.py --verify-only

      - name: Build Rust port (release)
        run: cargo build --release

      - name: Test shellcheck-rs
        run: cargo test -p shellcheck-rs

      - name: Test shellcheck-cli
        run: cargo test -p shellcheck-cli

      - name: Conformance gate
        run: cargo conformance-gate

      - name: Differential fuzz
        env: { "${{ insert }}": "${{ fromJSON(vars.FUZZ) }}" }
        run: cargo conformance-fuzz

  validity-smoke:
    name: Validity smoke
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: *CO

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: *rust

      - name: Build two cells
        run: cargo validity build --cell bash:5.3 --cell dash:0.5.13

      - name: Run two cells
        run: cargo validity --cell bash:5.3 --cell dash:0.5.13

name: Shell images and validity

on:
  schedule: [{ cron: "0 4 * * 1" }]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      rebuild-all:
        description: Rebuild every shell image even when its OCI image exists
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  push: { branches: [master, "!validity/*"] }
  pull_request:
    branches-ignore: ["validity/*"]
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/shells.yml"
      - "docker/shells/**"
      - "validity/**"
      - "crates/conformance/**"
      - "tools/affected_shell_cells.py"
      - "tools/test_affected_shell_cells.py"
      - "Cargo.toml"
      - "Cargo.lock"
      - ".cargo/**"

permissions: { contents: read }

jobs:
  pin:
    name: Pin sources
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.head_ref != 'validity/drift'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs: { cells: "${{ steps.cells.outputs.cells }}" }
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: &CO actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
        with: { fetch-depth: 0 }

      - name: Test affected-cell selection
        run: python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_affected_shell_cells.py

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: &RUST dtolnay/rust-toolchain@b725eda525362e7cf34af9a7243cac1e3f01a7ec # stable

      - name: Pin sources
        run: cargo validity pin

      - name: Plan image builds
        id: cells
        env:
          PLAN_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
          REBUILD_ALL: ${{ inputs.rebuild-all || false }}
        run: |
          if [[ "${REBUILD_ALL}" == "true" ]]; then
            cells="$(cargo validity cells)"
          elif [[ -n "${PLAN_BASE}" && ! "${PLAN_BASE}" =~ ^0+$ ]]; then
            if git cat-file -e "${PLAN_BASE}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null ||
              git fetch --no-tags origin "${PLAN_BASE}"; then
              cells="$(python3 tools/affected_shell_cells.py --base "${PLAN_BASE}")"
            else
              echo "::warning::Comparison commit ${PLAN_BASE} is unavailable; rebuilding all shell cells."
              cells="$(cargo validity cells)"
            fi
          else
            cells="$(python3 tools/affected_shell_cells.py)"
          fi
          echo "cells=${cells}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
          echo "Selected shell cells: ${cells}"

      - name: Upload matrix
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with: { name: matrix, path: validity/matrix.toml }

  build:
    name: "Build ${{ matrix.cell }}"
    needs: pin
    if: needs.pin.outputs.cells != '[]'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: { contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write, attestations: write }
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix: { cell: "${{ fromJSON(needs.pin.outputs.cells) }}" }
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: *CO

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: *RUST

      - name: Download matrix
        uses: &DL actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8
        with: { name: matrix, path: validity }

      - name: Set up buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@f87e5991a6d7451dcb8d9637bfbc97413f497069 # v4

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        uses: &LOGIN docker/login-action@8aa5831fb8d48d8f76594c7ddde61ae58019f550 # v4.8.0
        with: { registry: ghcr.io, username: "${{ github.actor }}", password: "${{ github.token }}" }

      - name: Build image
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env: &cell { cell: "${{ matrix.cell }}" }
        run: cargo validity build --cell "${cell}"

      - name: Build and push image
        id: push
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        env: *cell
        run: cargo validity build --push --cell "${cell}"

      - name: Record image digest
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        env:
          repository: ${{ steps.push.outputs.repository }}
          digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}
          index: ${{ strategy.job-index }}
        run: printf '%s  %s\n' "${digest#sha256:}" "${repository}" > "${index}.sha256"

      - name: Upload image digest
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7
        with: { name: "digest-${{ strategy.job-index }}", path: "${{ strategy.job-index }}.sha256" }

      - name: Generate image SBOM
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: anchore/sbom-action@66cbf4bc1f1c0d2edc94016e65bc221b6bb0ad6c # v0.24.3
        env:
          SYFT_SOURCE_NAME: ${{ matrix.cell }}
        with:
          image: "${{ steps.push.outputs.repository }}@${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}"
          format: spdx-json
          syft-version: v1.54.0
          output-file: image.spdx.json
          upload-artifact: false
          upload-release-assets: false
          dependency-snapshot: false

      - name: Attest image SBOM
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/attest@4d7d407517fe0a9f57ab8ca277dfd2efb1188c7f # main
        with:
          subject-name: "${{ steps.push.outputs.repository }}"
          subject-digest: "${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }}"
          sbom-path: image.spdx.json
          push-to-registry: false

  attest:
    name: Attest build provenance
    needs: build
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.build.result != 'skipped' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write, attestations: write }
    steps:
      - name: Download image digests
        uses: *DL
        with: { pattern: "digest-*", merge-multiple: true, path: digests }

      - name: Collect subjects
        run: cat digests/*.sha256 > subjects.sha256

      - name: Attest build provenance
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4
        with: { subject-checksums: subjects.sha256 }

  run:
    name: Run the matrix
    needs: [pin, build]
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && needs.pin.result == 'success' && (needs.build.result == 'success' || needs.build.result == 'skipped') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions: { contents: write, pull-requests: write, packages: read, id-token: write }
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: *CO

      - name: Install Rust stable
        uses: *RUST

      - name: Download matrix
        uses: *DL
        with: { name: matrix, path: validity }

      - name: Log in to GHCR
        uses: *LOGIN
        with: { registry: ghcr.io, username: "${{ github.actor }}", password: "${{ github.token }}" }

      - name: Open /dev/kvm to every user
        run: echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules;
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules;
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm

      - name: Pin rebuilt image digests
        if: needs.pin.outputs.cells != '[]'
        env: { CELLS: "${{ needs.pin.outputs.cells }}" }
        run: |
          mapfile -t cells < <(jq -r '.[] | "--cell=" + .' <<< "${CELLS}")
          cargo validity pin "${cells[@]}"

      - name: Record outcomes
        run: cargo validity --record

      - name: Refresh behaviour snapshot
        run: cargo conformance-snapshot --write

      - name: Obtain the Beepboop App identity and repository token
        uses: kjanat/beepboop/actions/token@v1
        id: beepboop
        with:
          permission-contents: write
          permission-pull-requests: write

      - name: Record validity drift
        uses: actions/github-script@3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3 # v9
        env:
          "${{ insert }}": ${{ steps.beepboop.outputs }}
          DRIFT_BRANCH: validity/drift
          PR_TITLE: "🧪 Record shell validity drift"
        with:
          github-token: ${{ steps.beepboop.outputs.token }}
          retries: 3
          script: |
            const paths = ['validity/matrix.toml', 'validity/outcomes.toml', 'validity/REPORT.md', 'crates/shellcheck-rs/src/dialect_rules.rs', 'rust/snapshot.txt'];
            const changed = (await exec.getExecOutput('git', ['diff', '--name-only', '--', ...paths], { silent: true })).stdout.trim().split('\n').filter(Boolean);
            if (!changed.length) return core.info('No validity drift.');

            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
            const branch = process.env.DRIFT_BRANCH;
            const title = process.env.PR_TITLE;
            const stat = (await exec.getExecOutput('git', ['diff', '--stat', '--', ...paths], { silent: true })).stdout.trim();
            const meaning = {
              'validity/matrix.toml': '**Image matrix:** resolved OCI digests or pinned build inputs changed.',
              'validity/outcomes.toml': '**Observed behavior:** at least one diagnostic/shell outcome changed.',
              'validity/REPORT.md': '**Rendered report:** the human-readable validity matrix was regenerated.',
              'crates/shellcheck-rs/src/dialect_rules.rs': '**Dialect rules:** the codes an added dialect keeps changed.',
              'rust/snapshot.txt': '**Behaviour snapshot:** the port output for an added dialect changed with its rules.',
            };
            const root = `${process.env.GITHUB_SERVER_URL}/${process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}`;
            const body = [
              '## 🧪 Shell validity drift', '',
              `The full shell fleet completed for [${context.sha.slice(0, 12)}](${root}/commit/${context.sha}) in [workflow run ${process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ID}](${root}/actions/runs/${process.env.GITHUB_RUN_ID}).`, '',
              '### What changed', ...changed.map(path => `- ${meaning[path]}`), '',
              '### Diff footprint', '', '```text', stat, '```', '',
              `Start with [the rendered report](${root}/blob/${branch}/validity/REPORT.md), then inspect the exact rows in the files tab.`,
            ].join('\n');

            for (const args of [
              ['config', 'user.name', process.env['bot-login']],
              ['config', 'user.email', process.env['bot-email']],
              ['switch', '--create', branch], ['add', '--', ...paths], ['commit', '--message', title],
            ]) await exec.exec('git', args);
            const remote = (await exec.getExecOutput('git', ['ls-remote', '--heads', 'origin', `refs/heads/${branch}`], { silent: true })).stdout.trim().split(/\s+/)[0];
            const lease = remote ? [`--force-with-lease=refs/heads/${branch}:${remote}`] : [];
            const origin = `https://x-access-token:${process.env.token}@github.com/${owner}/${repo}.git`;
            await exec.exec('git', ['-c', 'http.https://github.com/.extraheader=', 'push', ...lease, origin, `HEAD:refs/heads/${branch}`]);

            const common = { owner, repo };
            const [existing] = (await github.rest.pulls.list({ ...common, head: `${owner}:${branch}`, state: 'open', per_page: 1 })).data;
            const pull = existing
              ? (await github.rest.pulls.update({ ...common, pull_number: existing.number, title, body })).data
              : (await github.rest.pulls.create({ ...common, base: 'master', head: branch, title, body })).data;
            await Promise.all([
              github.rest.issues.addAssignees({ ...common, issue_number: pull.number, assignees: [owner] }),
              github.rest.issues.addLabels({ ...common, issue_number: pull.number, labels: ['conformance'] }),
            ]);

      - name: Test the recorded rules
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked --lib --bins

          retention-days: 14

# rshellcheck — [ShellCheck](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck "koalaman/shellcheck") in Rust

ShellCheck is a GPLv3 tool that gives warnings and suggestions for bash/sh shell scripts:

![Screenshot of a terminal showing problematic shell script lines highlighted](doc/terminal.png)

The goals of ShellCheck are

- To point out and clarify typical beginner's syntax issues that cause a shell
  to give cryptic error messages.

- To point out and clarify typical intermediate level semantic problems that
  cause a shell to behave strangely and counter-intuitively.

- To point out subtle caveats, corner cases and pitfalls that may cause an
  advanced user's otherwise working script to fail under future circumstances.

See [the gallery of bad code](README.md#user-content-gallery-of-bad-code) for examples of what ShellCheck can help you identify!

## How to use

There are a number of ways to use ShellCheck!

### On the web

Paste a shell script on <https://www.shellcheck.net> for instant feedback.

[ShellCheck.net](https://www.shellcheck.net) is always synchronized to the latest git commit, and is the easiest way to give ShellCheck a go. Tell your friends!

### From your terminal

Run `shellcheck yourscript` in your terminal for instant output, as seen above.

When checking multiple regular files, `rshellcheck` uses up to four available CPUs
by default. Set `-j N` (or `--jobs N`) to choose the worker count; `-j 1`
forces serial analysis. Quiet mode and invocations containing non-regular inputs
remain serial. Diagnostics retain input order. More workers can increase peak memory.

### In your editor

You can see ShellCheck suggestions directly in a variety of editors.

- Vim, through [ALE](https://github.com/w0rp/ale), [Neomake](https://github.com/neomake/neomake), or [Syntastic](https://github.com/scrooloose/syntastic):

![Screenshot of Vim showing inlined shellcheck feedback](doc/vim-syntastic.png).

- Emacs, through [Flycheck](https://github.com/flycheck/flycheck) or [Flymake](https://github.com/federicotdn/flymake-shellcheck):

![Screenshot of emacs showing inlined shellcheck feedback](doc/emacs-flycheck.png).

- Sublime, through [SublimeLinter](https://github.com/SublimeLinter/SublimeLinter-shellcheck).

- Pulsar Edit (former Atom), through [linter-shellcheck-pulsar](https://github.com/pulsar-cooperative/linter-shellcheck-pulsar).

- VSCode, through [vscode-shellcheck](https://github.com/timonwong/vscode-shellcheck).

- Most other editors, through [GCC error compatibility](shellcheck.1.md#user-content-formats).

### In your build or test suites

While ShellCheck is mostly intended for interactive use, it can easily be added to builds or test suites.
It makes canonical use of exit codes, so you can just add a `shellcheck` command as part of the process.

For example, in a Makefile:

```Makefile
check-scripts:
    # Fail if any of these files have warnings
    shellcheck myscripts/*.sh
```

or in a Travis CI `.travis.yml` file:

```yaml
script:
  # Fail if any of these files have warnings
  - shellcheck myscripts/*.sh
```

Services and platforms that have ShellCheck pre-installed and ready to use:

- [Travis CI](https://travis-ci.org/)
- [Codacy](https://www.codacy.com/)
- [Code Climate](https://codeclimate.com/)
- [Code Factor](https://www.codefactor.io/)
- [Codety](https://www.codety.io/) via the [Codety Scanner](https://github.com/codetyio/codety-scanner)
- [CircleCI](https://circleci.com) via the [ShellCheck Orb](https://circleci.com/orbs/registry/orb/circleci/shellcheck)
- [Github](https://github.com/features/actions) (only Linux)
- [Trunk Code Quality](https://trunk.io/code-quality) (universal linter; [allows you to explicitly version your shellcheck install](https://github.com/trunk-io/plugins/blob/bcbb361dcdbe4619af51ea7db474d7fb87540d20/.trunk/trunk.yaml#L32)) via the [shellcheck plugin](https://github.com/trunk-io/plugins/blob/main/linters/shellcheck/plugin.yaml)
- [CodeRabbit](https://coderabbit.ai/)

Most other services, including [GitLab](https://about.gitlab.com/), let you install
ShellCheck yourself, either through the system's package manager (see [Installing](#installing)),
or by downloading and unpacking a [binary release](#installing-a-pre-compiled-binary).

It's a good idea to manually install a specific ShellCheck version regardless. This avoids
any surprise build breaks when a new version with new warnings is published.

For customized filtering or reporting, ShellCheck can output simple JSON, CheckStyle compatible XML,
GCC compatible warnings as well as human readable text (with or without ANSI colors). See the
[Integration](https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/wiki/Integration) wiki page for more documentation.

## Installing

The easiest way to install ShellCheck locally is through your package manager.

To install this Rust port from git:

```sh
cargo install --locked --git 'https://github.com/kjanat/shellcheck-rs' 'shellcheck-cli' --bin 'rshellcheck'
```

For GitHub Actions, use this repository's setup action to install `rshellcheck`:

```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v6
  - uses: kjanat/shellcheck-rs@master
    with:
      version: "1.0.0" # Omit to install the latest stable release.
  - run: rshellcheck scripts/example.sh
```

The action downloads a native release binary, verifies its SHA-256 checksum, and
adds it to `PATH`. It supports Linux (x64, x86, ARM64, ARMv7), macOS (x64, ARM64),
and Windows (x64, x86, ARM64). No Rust toolchain is needed. Self-hosted runners
need Bash, GitHub CLI (`gh`), `tar` (Unix) or `unzip` and `cygpath` (Windows), and
`sha256sum` or `shasum`. The `token` input defaults to `${{ github.token }}`;
the `version` and `path` outputs report the installed version and binary directory.
The action reference selects the installer code; the `version` input selects the
binary release. Pin the action to a commit SHA for reproducible workflows.

### pre-commit

To run ShellCheck via [pre-commit](https://pre-commit.com/), add the hook to your `.pre-commit-config.yaml`:

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck-precommit
    rev: v0.11.0
    hooks:
      - id: shellcheck
        # args: ["--severity=warning"]  # Optionally only show errors and warnings
```

### Travis CI

Travis CI has now integrated ShellCheck by default, so you don't need to manually install it.

If you still want to do so in order to upgrade at your leisure or ensure you're
using the latest release, follow the steps below to install a binary version.

### Installing a pre-compiled binary

The pre-compiled binaries come in `tar.xz` files. To decompress them, make sure `xz` is installed.
On Debian/Ubuntu/Mint, you can `apt install xz-utils`.
On Redhat/Fedora/CentOS, `yum -y install xz`.

A simple installer may do something like:

```bash
scversion="stable" # or "v0.4.7", or "latest"
wget -qO- "https://github.com/koalaman/shellcheck/releases/download/${scversion?}/shellcheck-${scversion?}.linux.x86_64.tar.xz" | tar -xJv
cp "shellcheck-${scversion}/shellcheck" /usr/bin/
shellcheck --version
```

## Compiling from source

The CLI and analysis library build with Rust; no Haskell toolchain is required.

```sh
cargo build --release --locked -p shellcheck-cli
cargo test --workspace --locked --lib --bins
cargo conformance-snapshot
```

Native Python wheels install the same CLI with `uv tool install rshellcheck`; see
[native Python packaging](bindings/native/python/README.md).

The executable is `target/release/rshellcheck`. See [WASM bindings](bindings/wasm/README.md)
for Go, Python and JavaScript/browser embedding and workspace setup.

Conformance against upstream is optional locally and required in CI. With GHC,
Cabal and authenticated `gh` available, run:

```sh
python tools/oracle.py
cargo conformance-gate
cargo conformance-fuzz
```

The helper fetches the exact revision in [tools/oracle.json](tools/oracle.json)
into `.cache/upstream-shellcheck` and builds `.cache/shellcheck-oracle`.
Haskell source and build products remain in ignored cache directories.
See [UPSTREAM.md](UPSTREAM.md) for provenance and intentional differences.

## Gallery of bad code

So what kind of things does ShellCheck look for? Here is an incomplete list of detected issues.

### Quoting

ShellCheck can recognize several types of incorrect quoting:

```sh
echo $1                           # Unquoted variables
find . -name *.ogg                # Unquoted find/grep patterns
rm "~/my file.txt"                # Quoted tilde expansion
v='--verbose="true"'; cmd $v      # Literal quotes in variables
for f in "*.ogg"                  # Incorrectly quoted 'for' loops
touch $@                          # Unquoted $@
echo 'Don't forget to restart!'   # Singlequote closed by apostrophe
echo 'Don\'t try this at home'    # Attempting to escape ' in ''
echo 'Path is $PATH'              # Variables in single quotes
trap "echo Took ${SECONDS}s" 0    # Prematurely expanded trap
unset var[i]                      # Array index treated as glob
```

### Conditionals

ShellCheck can recognize many types of incorrect test statements.

```sh
[[ n != 0 ]]                      # Constant test expressions
[[ -e *.mpg ]]                    # Existence checks of globs
[[ $foo==0 ]]                     # Always true due to missing spaces
[[ -n "$foo " ]]                  # Always true due to literals
[[ $foo =~ "fo+" ]]               # Quoted regex in =~
[ foo =~ re ]                     # Unsupported [ ] operators
[ $1 -eq "shellcheck" ]           # Numerical comparison of strings
[ $n && $m ]                      # && in [ .. ]
[ grep -q foo file ]              # Command without $(..)
[[ "$$file" == *.jpg ]]           # Comparisons that can't succeed
(( 1 -lt 2 ))                     # Using test operators in ((..))
[ x ] & [ y ] | [ z ]             # Accidental backgrounding and piping
```

### Frequently misused commands

ShellCheck can recognize instances where commands are used incorrectly:

```sh
grep '*foo*' file                 # Globs in regex contexts
find . -exec foo {} && bar {} \;  # Prematurely terminated find -exec
sudo echo 'Var=42' > /etc/profile # Redirecting sudo
time --format=%s sleep 10         # Passing time(1) flags to time builtin
while read h; do ssh "$h" uptime  # Commands eating while loop input
alias archive='mv $1 /backup'     # Defining aliases with arguments
tr -cd '[a-zA-Z0-9]'              # [] around ranges in tr
exec foo; echo "Done!"            # Misused 'exec'
find -name \*.bak -o -name \*~ -delete  # Implicit precedence in find
# find . -exec foo > bar \;       # Redirections in find
f() { whoami; }; sudo f           # External use of internal functions
```

### Common beginner's mistakes

ShellCheck recognizes many common beginner's syntax errors:

```sh
var = 42                          # Spaces around = in assignments
$foo=42                           # $ in assignments
for $var in *; do ...             # $ in for loop variables
var$n="Hello"                     # Wrong indirect assignment
echo ${var$n}                     # Wrong indirect reference
var=(1, 2, 3)                     # Comma separated arrays
array=( [index] = value )         # Incorrect index initialization
echo $var[14]                     # Missing {} in array references
echo "Argument 10 is $10"         # Positional parameter misreference
if $(myfunction); then ..; fi     # Wrapping commands in $()
else if othercondition; then ..   # Using 'else if'
f; f() { echo "hello world; }     # Using function before definition
[ false ]                         # 'false' being true
if ( -f file )                    # Using (..) instead of test
```

### Style

ShellCheck can make suggestions to improve style:

```sh
[[ -z $(find /tmp | grep mpg) ]]  # Use grep -q instead
a >> log; b >> log; c >> log      # Use a redirection block instead
echo "The time is `date`"         # Use $() instead
cd dir; process *; cd ..;         # Use subshells instead
echo $[1+2]                       # Use standard $((..)) instead of old $[]
echo $(($RANDOM % 6))             # Don't use $ on variables in $((..))
echo "$(date)"                    # Useless use of echo
cat file | grep foo               # Useless use of cat
```

### Data and typing errors

ShellCheck can recognize issues related to data and typing:

```sh
args="$@"                         # Assigning arrays to strings
files=(foo bar); echo "$files"    # Referencing arrays as strings
declare -A arr=(foo bar)          # Associative arrays without index
printf "%s\n" "Arguments: $@."    # Concatenating strings and arrays
[[ $# > 2 ]]                      # Comparing numbers as strings
var=World; echo "Hello " var      # Unused lowercase variables
echo "Hello $name"                # Unassigned lowercase variables
cmd | read bar; echo $bar         # Assignments in subshells
cat foo | cp bar                  # Piping to commands that don't read
printf '%s: %s\n' foo             # Mismatches in printf argument count
eval "${array[@]}"                # Lost word boundaries in array eval
for i in "${x[@]}"; do ${x[$i]}   # Using array value as key
```

### Robustness

ShellCheck can make suggestions for improving the robustness of a script:

```sh
rm -rf "$STEAMROOT/"*            # Catastrophic rm
touch ./-l; ls *                 # Globs that could become options
find . -exec sh -c 'a && b {}' \; # Find -exec shell injection
printf "Hello $name"             # Variables in printf format
for f in $(ls *.txt); do         # Iterating over ls output
export MYVAR=$(cmd)              # Masked exit codes
case $version in 2.*) :;; 2.6.*) # Shadowed case branches
```

### Portability

ShellCheck will warn when using features not supported by the shebang. For example, if you set the shebang to `#!/bin/sh`, ShellCheck will warn about portability issues similar to `checkbashisms`:

```sh
echo {1..$n}                     # Works in ksh, but not bash/dash/sh
echo {1..10}                     # Works in ksh and bash, but not dash/sh
echo -n 42                       # Works in ksh, bash and dash, undefined in sh
expr match str regex             # Unportable alias for `expr str : regex`
trap 'exit 42' sigint            # Unportable signal spec
cmd &> file                      # Unportable redirection operator
read foo < /dev/tcp/host/22      # Unportable intercepted files
foo-bar() { ..; }                # Undefined/unsupported function name
[ $UID = 0 ]                     # Variable undefined in dash/sh
local var=value                  # local is undefined in sh
time sleep 1 | sleep 5           # Undefined uses of 'time'
```

### Miscellaneous

ShellCheck recognizes a menagerie of other issues:

```sh
PS1='\e[0;32m\$\e[0m '            # PS1 colors not in \[..\]
PATH="$PATH:~/bin"                # Literal tilde in $PATH
rm “file”                         # Unicode quotes
echo "Hello world"                # Carriage return / DOS line endings
echo hello \                      # Trailing spaces after \
var=42 echo $var                  # Expansion of inlined environment
!# bin/bash -x -e                 # Common shebang errors
echo $((n/180*100))               # Unnecessary loss of precision
ls *[:digit:].txt                 # Bad character class globs
sed 's/foo/bar/' file > file      # Redirecting to input
var2=$var2                        # Variable assigned to itself
[ x$var = xval ]                  # Antiquated x-comparisons
ls() { ls -l "$@"; }              # Infinitely recursive wrapper
alias ls='ls -l'; ls foo          # Alias used before it takes effect
for x; do for x; do               # Nested loop uses same variable
while getopts "a" f; do case $f in "b") # Unhandled getopts flags
```

"""Reusable, serialized ShellCheck instance; no WASI or filesystem imports."""

import json
from collections.abc import Mapping
from importlib.resources import files
from threading import Lock
from typing import cast, final

import wasmtime

type JSON = bool | int | float | str | list[JSON] | dict[str, JSON] | None


def _export[T: (wasmtime.Func, wasmtime.Memory)](
    exports: Mapping[str, object], name: str, kind: type[T]
) -> T:
    value = exports[name]
    if not isinstance(value, kind):
        raise TypeError(f"WASM export {name} is not a {kind.__name__}")
    return value


def _call_u32(func: wasmtime.Func, store: wasmtime.Store, *args: int) -> int:
    value = cast(object, func(store, *args))
    if not isinstance(value, int):
        raise TypeError("WASM export returned a non-integer")
    return value & 0xFFFFFFFF


@final
class Checker:
    def __init__(self, wasm: bytes | None = None, *, fuel: int = 1_000_000_000):
        if wasm is None:
            wasm = (
                files("rshellcheck_wasm_data")
                .joinpath("shellcheck_wasm.wasm")
                .read_bytes()
            )
        config = wasmtime.Config()
        config.consume_fuel = True
        self._engine = wasmtime.Engine(config)
        self._module = wasmtime.Module(self._engine, wasm)
        if self._module.imports:
            raise ValueError("Unexpected WASM imports")
        self._store = wasmtime.Store(self._engine)
        self._store.set_fuel(fuel)
        exports = wasmtime.Instance(self._store, self._module, []).exports(self._store)
        self._memory = _export(exports, "memory", wasmtime.Memory)
        self._prepare = _export(exports, "sc_prepare", wasmtime.Func)
        self._check = _export(exports, "sc_check", wasmtime.Func)
        self._output_len = _export(exports, "sc_output_len", wasmtime.Func)
        abi_version = _export(exports, "sc_abi_version", wasmtime.Func)
        if _call_u32(abi_version, self._store) != 1:
            raise ValueError("Unsupported ShellCheck ABI")
        self._fuel = fuel
        self._closed = False
        self._lock = Lock()

    def check(self, request: dict[str, JSON]) -> dict[str, JSON]:
        data = json.dumps(request, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
        if len(data) > 16 * 1024 * 1024:
            raise ValueError("Request exceeds 16 MiB")
        with self._lock:
            if self._closed:
                raise RuntimeError("Checker closed; create a new instance")
            store = self._store
            try:
                store.set_fuel(self._fuel)
                ptr = _call_u32(self._prepare, store, len(data))
                if not ptr:
                    raise RuntimeError("Request rejected")
                _ = self._memory.write(store, data, ptr)
                ptr = _call_u32(self._check, store)
                size = _call_u32(self._output_len, store)
                output = bytes(self._memory.read(store, ptr, ptr + size))
                result = cast(JSON, json.loads(output))
            except Exception:
                self._closed = True
                store.close()
                raise
            if not isinstance(result, dict):
                raise TypeError("ShellCheck result is not a JSON object")
            if "error" in result:
                raise ValueError(result["error"])
            return result

    def close(self) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            if not self._closed:
                self._store.close()
            self._closed = True

    def __enter__(self) -> "Checker":
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:
        self.close()

"""Fetch and build the exact upstream oracle outside the tracked source tree."""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import TypedDict, cast

type JSON = bool | int | float | str | list[JSON] | dict[str, JSON] | None
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
CACHE = ROOT / ".cache"
SOURCE = CACHE / "upstream-shellcheck"
BINARY = CACHE / "shellcheck-oracle"


class Pin(TypedDict):
    repository: str
    revision: str
    version: str


class Args(argparse.Namespace):
    fetch_only: bool = False
    verify_only: bool = False


def run(*args: str, cwd: Path = ROOT) -> str:
    return subprocess.check_output(args, cwd=cwd, text=True).strip()


def load_json(path: Path) -> JSON:
    return cast(JSON, json.loads(path.read_text()))


def load_pin() -> Pin:
    data = load_json(ROOT / "tools/oracle.json")
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise TypeError("Oracle pin must be a JSON object")
    repository, revision, version = (
        data.get("repository"),
        data.get("revision"),
        data.get("version"),
    )
    if not (
        isinstance(repository, str)
        and isinstance(revision, str)
        and isinstance(version, str)
    ):
        raise TypeError("Oracle pin needs string repository, revision and version")
    return {"repository": repository, "revision": revision, "version": version}


def prepare() -> Pin:
    pin = load_pin()
    revision = pin["revision"]
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", revision):
        raise ValueError("Oracle revision must be a full commit SHA")
    CACHE.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if not SOURCE.exists():
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="oracle-fetch-", dir=CACHE) as tmp:
            checkout = Path(tmp) / "source"
            _ = run(
                "gh",
                "repo",
                "clone",
                pin["repository"],
                str(checkout),
                "--",
                "--filter=blob:none",
                "--no-checkout",
                "--depth=1",
            )
            _ = run("git", "fetch", "--depth=1", "origin", revision, cwd=checkout)
            _ = run("git", "checkout", "--detach", revision, cwd=checkout)
            _ = checkout.rename(SOURCE)
    if run("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD", cwd=SOURCE) != revision:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{SOURCE} has a different revision; preserve it elsewhere before fetching"
        )
    if run("git", "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=normal", cwd=SOURCE):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{SOURCE} has local changes; refusing to use a modified oracle"
        )
    return pin


def verify(pin: Pin) -> None:
    metadata = load_json(CACHE / "shellcheck-oracle.json")
    expected = {**pin, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(BINARY.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    if metadata != expected:
        raise ValueError("Cached oracle does not match pinned source and binary digest")


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    _ = parser.add_argument("--fetch-only", action="store_true")
    _ = parser.add_argument("--verify-only", action="store_true")
    args = parser.parse_args(namespace=Args())
    pin = prepare()
    print(f"Oracle source: {SOURCE} at {pin['revision']}", flush=True)
    if args.fetch_only:
        return
    if args.verify_only:
        verify(pin)
        print("Cached oracle identity verified")
        return
    _ = subprocess.run(["cabal", "build", "exe:shellcheck"], cwd=SOURCE, check=True)

    metadata = {**pin, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(BINARY.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    _ = (CACHE / "shellcheck-oracle.json").write_text(
        json.dumps(metadata, indent=2) + "\n"
    )
    print(f"Oracle built: {BINARY}")

"""Reject stale or modified oracle caches instead of silently accepting parity."""

import hashlib
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

import oracle


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Layout:
    cache: Path
    binary: Path
    pin: oracle.Pin


class OracleTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def layout(self) -> Layout:
        tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(tmp.cleanup)
        root = Path(tmp.name)
        cache = root / ".cache"
        source = cache / "upstream-shellcheck"
        source.mkdir(parents=True)
        (root / "tools").mkdir()
        pin: oracle.Pin = {
            "revision": "a" * 40,
            "repository": "koalaman/shellcheck",
            "version": "0.11.0",
        }
        _ = (root / "tools/oracle.json").write_text(json.dumps(pin))
        binary = cache / "shellcheck-oracle"
        for name, value in [
            ("ROOT", root),
            ("CACHE", cache),
            ("SOURCE", source),
            ("BINARY", binary),
        ]:
            mock = patch.object(oracle, name, value)
            _ = mock.start()
            self.addCleanup(mock.stop)
        return Layout(cache, binary, pin)

    def test_matching_clean_checkout(self):
        pin = self.layout().pin
        with patch.object(oracle, "run", side_effect=[pin["revision"], ""]):
            self.assertEqual(oracle.prepare(), pin)

    def test_wrong_revision_is_not_overwritten(self):
        _ = self.layout()
        with (
            patch.object(oracle, "run", return_value="b" * 40),
            self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "different revision"),
        ):
            _ = oracle.prepare()

    def test_modified_source_is_rejected(self):
        pin = self.layout().pin
        with (
            patch.object(
                oracle,
                "run",
                side_effect=[pin["revision"], " M src/ShellCheck/Parser.hs"],
            ),
            self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "local changes"),
        ):
            _ = oracle.prepare()

    def test_binary_digest_and_source_pin_are_checked(self):
        layout = self.layout()
        _ = layout.binary.write_bytes(b"oracle")
        metadata = {**layout.pin, "sha256": hashlib.sha256(b"oracle").hexdigest()}
        _ = (layout.cache / "shellcheck-oracle.json").write_text(json.dumps(metadata))
        oracle.verify(layout.pin)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "does not match"):
            oracle.verify({**layout.pin, "revision": "b" * 40})
        _ = layout.binary.write_bytes(b"stale oracle")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "does not match"):
            oracle.verify(layout.pin)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _ = unittest.main()
